event.title: TikTok to Pay $400 Million in Landmark Children's Privacy Settlement
event.canonical_title: TikTok to Pay $400 Million in Landmark Children's Privacy Settlement
event.summary: TikTok has agreed to a $400 million settlement with the US Department of Justice following allegations that it violated children's online privacy laws. The lawsuit, filed in 2024, accused TikTok and its parent company ByteDance of collecting extensive data from users under the age of 13 without parental consent. The settlement is considered one of the largest of its kind in the United States.

timeline.title: TikTok Settles $400 Million Lawsuit Over Children's Privacy Violations
timeline.summary: TikTok has agreed to a $400 million settlement with the US Department of Justice regarding allegations of violating children's privacy laws. The settlement includes an immediate payment of $300 million, with an additional $100 million to be paid after the vacating of a prior consent decree against its predecessor, Musical.ly. This agreement follows a lawsuit filed in 2024, which claimed that TikTok and its parent company, ByteDance, collected extensive data from users under the age of 13.

event_overview.title: About Children's Privacy Lawsuit
event_overview.subject: Children's Privacy Lawsuit
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a U.S. civil children’s-privacy case in which the Department of Justice, acting after a Federal Trade Commission referral, alleged that TikTok and ByteDance violated the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA). The litigation ended in an announced August 2026 settlement; the government stated that the claims were allegations and that there had been no determination of liability.

facts.label: Case timeline
facts.value: The United States filed the lawsuit on August 2, 2024; the Justice Department announced the settlement on August 21, 2026.

facts.label: Parties and forum
facts.value: The case was brought by the United States against ByteDance, TikTok, and affiliated entities in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, Civil Action No. 2:24-cv-06535.

facts.label: Legal scope
facts.value: The case concerned COPPA and its implementing rule, which generally require online services to give notice to and obtain parental consent before knowingly collecting, using, or disclosing personal information from children under 13; the government also alleged noncompliance with a prior order involving TikTok’s predecessor, Musical.ly.

facts.label: Government allegations
facts.value: The 2024 complaint alleged that TikTok allowed children under 13 to use regular accounts, collected and retained their personal information without required parental notice or consent, and often failed to honor parents’ requests to delete accounts and data.

facts.label: Settlement structure
facts.value: According to the Justice Department, TikTok is to pay $300 million immediately and a further $100 million if a court enters an order vacating the earlier Musical.ly consent decree; DOJ described the resolution as one of the largest recoveries in a COPPA case.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the August 2026 settlement news, not the full history of COPPA enforcement against TikTok/Musical.ly or other children’s-privacy litigation.
